column1: # THE HOUSE JACOB LEIBHOLZ WAS DEPORTED FROM, AND ITS OWNER DISAPPEARS OUT OF IT IN PRINT.
# Berliner Adressbuch, Teil IV (Straßenteil), ZLB 34115495, volumes 1939 to 1943, read at the page
# image and in the page text. Row 203. Read 11 October 2026.
# WHY IT WAS RUN. Jacob Leibholz is on the 30th Osttransport of 26 February 1943 at
# TREUCHTLINGERSTRASSE 4, Berlin-Schöneberg, and the AJDC card adds "b/SPIER" — lodging with a
# family called Spier. The 1939 census has him at MERANER STRASSE 2 with Auguste and Siegfried.
# Row 203 wanted the Spier household found. It is found, and the house turned out to say more.
field
# ---------------- THE ANSWER TO THE ROW'S QUESTION ----------------
*** SPIER, H., HANDELSVERTRETER, WITH A TELEPHONE, AT TREUCHTLINGER STRASSE 2.4 ***
column2: present in the 1940, 1941, 1942 AND 1943 volumes, the same line in all four: "Spier H., Handelsvertr. T." A Handelsvertreter is a commercial agent or sales representative. THAT IS THE HOUSEHOLD JACOB LODGED WITH, named by the directory three years before the transport and still named in the volume that was on the shelves when he was deported.

column1: and the house is 2 AND 4 TOGETHER, on a corner
column2: every volume prints the two numbers as one property — "2. 4" — and cross-references it: "geh. z. Barbarossastraße 36a" in 1940, "s. a. Barbarossastr. 36a" in 1941, and in 1939 ALSO "s. a. Luitpoldstr. 25". A transport list that says "Treuchtlingerstr. 4" and a directory that says "2. 4" are the same door.

column1: the other nine of the household, as the directory gives them in 1941
column2: Bayer, W., Oberstleutnant · Eberhardt, C., Kaufmann · Jakob, W., Maurer · KEPHAN, H. ISRAEL, Einrichter · Kochanowska, F., Hausgehilfin · Petras, M., kfm. Angestellter · Rosenstock, L., kfm. Angestellter · SPIER, H., Handelsvertreter · Voß, C. F., Kaufmann · Wendorf, R., Abteilungsleiter. A retired colonel, a bricklayer and a housemaid in the same list as a man carrying the compulsory name.

column1: # ---------------- AND THE SEQUENCE THE ROW DID NOT ASK FOR ----------------
*** FIVE VOLUMES OF ONE HOUSE, AND THE OWNER GOES FROM A NAME TO A NAME-PLUS-SARA TO NOBODY ***
column2: 1939: "E EISENBERG, G., Ww." — a widow, her own name and nothing else. 1940: "E EISENBERG, G. SARA, Ww. T." 1941: the same, "E Eisenberg, G. Sara, Ww. T." 1942: *** "E UNGENANNT." *** 1943: *** "E UNGENANNT." *** Owner named, owner named with the name the state imposed, and then no owner at all.

column1: what that is and what it is not
column2: THE DECREE OF 17 AUGUST 1938 required every Jewish woman whose forename was not on the approved list to add SARA, in force from 1 January 1939 — which is exactly why the 1939 volume, compiled from 1938 returns, does not carry it and the 1940 volume does. SO THE MIDDLE NAME DATES HER AS JEWISH ON THE STATE'S OWN RECORD. *** WHAT "E UNGENANNT" MEANS IS NOT PROVED HERE. *** It is the directory declining to name an owner. It is consistent with a forced sale, with a property under administration, with her death, and with an ordinary editorial gap. THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT KNOW WHICH and does not pretend to. What it records is that the house Jacob Leibholz was deported from had a named Jewish owner in the 1941 volume and no owner in the 1942 one.

column1: and one tenant leaves on the same page
column2: KEPHAN, H. ISRAEL, Einrichter, is in the 1940 and 1941 lists and is GONE FROM 1942 AND 1943 — the same volume boundary as the owner's name. Of the ten in the house, he is the only other one marked.

column1: *** AND SPIER IS NOT MARKED, IN ANY OF THE FOUR YEARS ***
column2: no "Israel" beside his name in 1940, 1941, 1942 or 1943, while the same page marks Eisenberg and Kephan and the same volume marks four men in one house round the corner in Martin-Luther-Straße — Hohmann, Marcuse, Sellen and Zepler, all "Israel", one of them a "jüd. Krankenbehandler". THE DIRECTORY'S MARKING IS WORKING ON THIS PAGE, SO ITS ABSENCE BESIDE SPIER IS EVIDENCE AND NOT SILENCE — the same reasoning this archive used for Günther Leibholz's "ev." in row 257. A Jewish man under transport order lodging in an unmarked household, in a house whose owner had been marked and has now vanished from the page.

column1: NOT CLAIMED
column2: that Spier hid him, sheltered him, or was paid. Forced relocation of Jewish households into designated rooms was ordinary administration in Berlin by 1942, and the AJDC's "b/Spier" records an address, not a kindness. The directory cannot tell those apart and neither can this file.

column1: # ---------------- THE INSTRUMENT, BECAUSE IT FAILED THE OBVIOUS WAY FIRST ----------------
*** THE STREET NAME IS MANGLED IN EVERY SINGLE VOLUME AND A FULL-TEXT SEARCH NEVER FINDS THE STREET PAGE ***
column2: the Teil IV headings OCR as "Tremhtliagrr Str." in 1942 and "Trerlchtlürger Str." in 1943. Searching the volume for "Treuchtlinger" returns 18 to 40 pages — EVERY ONE OF THEM A NAMENTEIL ENTRY of somebody who lived there, plus cross-references from other streets — AND NOT THE STREET'S OWN PAGE. This is the Dieffenbachstraße failure exactly: the 1941 OCR mangled that street to "Diessenbachsir" and the year was found only by reading the run in place.

column1: what works instead, and it is cheap
column2: WALK THE RUNNING HEADS OF TEIL IV. They survive the OCR far better than the body — "Schöneberg Tempelhofer Weg", "Schöneberg Vorbergstr.", "Schöneberg Wartburgstr." — so the alphabetical position of a street can be bracketed in five or six page reads and the page itself opened directly. Treuchtlinger Str. is at ORDER 5933 (1939), 6069 (1940), 6106 (1941), 6181 (1942), 6088 (1943).

column1: and the page geometry, for whoever comes next
column2: these Teil IV pages are SEVEN COLUMNS WIDE, about 331 px apart at a 4000 px render, text block roughly x=160 to x=2480. The column rules are printed lines and score as ink, so an ink profile will not find the gutters; divide the block instead.

column1: the row's first test is answered WITHOUT the instrument it proposed
column2: row 203 wanted Mapping the Lives searched by address, "the method that found the Danckelmannstraße household". That site's API needs authentication. THE ADRESSBUCH ANSWERED IT FOR NOTHING, and gave five years of the house instead of one snapshot.

column1: and the row's earlier negative is explained rather than overturned
column2: on 10 October a full-text sweep found "Spier" and "Treuchtlinger" co-occurring on three pages with no Spier at that address, and concluded the co-occurrence was PAGE-LEVEL, NOT ADDRESS-LEVEL. That was right, and the reason is now known: the street page the Spier entry sits on does not contain the string "Treuchtlinger" at all, because the heading is mangled. A search for both terms could never have found it.

column1: WHAT IS STILL OPEN
column2: WHEN Jacob moved from Meraner Straße 2 to Treuchtlinger Straße, and whether Auguste and Siegfried moved with him. The directory lists householders, not lodgers, so it will not show him at either address after 1939 and cannot answer this. The Schöneberg registration cards or the deportation file would.

column1: read at the image where it matters
column2: the 1941 and 1942 entries for house 2.4 were read at the page image at 3.3 and 3.4 times, including "E Eisenberg, G. Sara, Ww." and "2. 4 E ungenannt" — the two lines the whole sequence turns on. The 1939, 1940 and 1943 entries are from the page text and are marked as such; all three agree with the two that were read by eye on every name they share.

column1: source
column2: Zentral- und Landesbibliothek Berlin, digital.zlb.de, Berliner Adressbuch Teil IV, PI 34115495, volumes 1939 (order 5933), 1940 (6069), 1941 (6106), 1942 (6181) and 1943 (6088). Read 11 October 2026. No account, nothing purchased.
